Introduction:
States are currently experiencing workforce and budget strain with competing large scale IT projects including: NCPDP Telecommunication Standard Version update from D.0 to F6 compliance date of August 14, 2027, API from 2024 CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization (PA) Final Rule (CMS-0057-F) compliance date of January 1, 2027, and FDA transition from 11-digit NDC to 12-digit NDCs by March 7, 2033.
We request the deadline be delayed by 36 months for state Medicaid and CHIP FFS programs up front, rather than requiring more paperwork by having states apply for an extension for the implementation of the API for drugs, and NCPDP and FHIR standards.
We request funding assistance and support with vendor readiness and procurement.
NDPDP Standards for Electronic Prior Authorization for Pharmacy Drugs:
States need support in funding and procurement. North Dakota Medicaid does not have a Pharmacy Benefits Manager and operates a very small Fee-For-Service program. We currently do not support NCPDP SCRIPT, F&B, or RTPB standards. We have attempted to procure services for these in the past, but it has not been fruitful primarily due to lack of intermediary vendor willingness to respond to a Request for Proposal. Supporting these standards will require our prior authorization vendor to have connectivity with an electronic prior authorization intermediatory, which would require re-procurement and cost increase to the contract and vendor readiness to work with the state.
We currently do not have a budget for implementation of these standards and would not be able to meet the timeline proposed in this rule. North Dakota is currently in a budget shortfall, and the governor has ordered a 10% budget reduction to the North Dakota Department of Health and Human Services, so state funding may be difficult to secure. Our next legislative session concludes April 2027, and our following fiscal biennium starts July 2027. We would require a vendor procurement process until the end of September 2027. The soonest we could start work would be October 1, 2027, which is the compliance deadline. Following contracting, our vendor would need time for planning, development, and testing. The proposed rule offers an extension application process and acknowledges that states would be considered for an extension up to 36 months. Knowing the limitations state Medicaid programs face in meeting the proposed deadline, we request the deadline be delayed by 36 months for state Medicaid and CHIP FFS programs up front, rather than requiring more paperwork by having states apply for the extension.
We anticipate challenges meeting the large workload required to implement the questionnaires for all drugs that require prior authorization and continued maintenance. We are currently stretched very thin with pharmacy program staffing navigating the NCPDP D.0 to F6 transition, additional rebate review required with the GENEROUS model, and the WCAG 2.2 Guidelines compliance deadline of April 26, 2027.
Prior Authorization API for Drugs:
It is noted that the compliance date of October 1, 2027 rather than 3 years afforded under the 2024 CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule, because it would not require payer to build a new API and just add medical drugs into the existing workflow. There will be a considerably large effort for our prior authorization vendor to adopt the Prior Authorization API FHIR standards and have connectivity with the Prior Authorization API to report coverage and documentation requirements to support electronic prior authorization. This which likely require re-procurement and / or cost increase to the prior authorization vendor contract.
The compliance date for the API as required in the 2024 CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization (PA) Final Rule (CMS-0057-F) is January 1, 2027 so gathering information and planning will be very complicated while the API from CMS-0057-F is not yet built. The current compliance date only allows for 9 additional months for planning and building after the API compliance date in CMS-0057-F.
We will have increased state oversight and contracting requirements with our Managed Care plan to ensure compliance with the rule.
For the same reasons mentioned in the NCPDP Standards for ePA for Pharmacy Drugs section of this comment, we request the deadline be extended by 36 months for state Medicaid and CHIP FFS as well as assistance with funding and assessment of readiness for vendor procurement.
Implementation Guides for Interoperability APIs
The compliance date for the API as required in the 2024 CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization (PA) Final Rule (CMS-0057-F) is January 1, 2027 so gathering information and planning will be very complicated while the API from CMS-0057-F is not yet built. The current compliance date only allows for 9 additional months for planning and building after the API compliance date in CMS-0057-F.
Information about Prior Authorization for Drugs in the APIs:
Our prior authorization vendor would need to adopt the FHIR standards and have connectivity with the API to report prior authorization information within 1 business day. This would require re-procurement and cost increase to the contract. For the same reasons mentioned in the NCPDP Standards for ePA for Pharmacy Drugs section of this comment, we request the deadline be extended by 36 months for state Medicaid and CHIP FFS as well as assistance with funding and readiness for vendor procurement.
We request the requirement be changed to 2 business days. This would allow time to issue a determination on the prior authorization request which can be up to 24 hours and additionally, it would allow time for the information exchange will likely require a file transfer. The 1 business day requirement would be difficult to meet even with near real time information exchanges.
Our Managed Care plan processes our physician administered drug prior authorization requests for our Medicaid expansion population and similarly would require information exchange that would be difficult to meet within 1 business day.
We will have increased state oversight and contracting requirements with our Managed Care plan to ensure compliance with the rule.
Prior Authorization API Metrics for Drugs:
The API compliance date for drugs is currently October 1, 2027 with a 2028 start date for reporting API metric. We request the reporting implementation deadline be extended to the follow the first full year of API use. For example, the first report would be due March 2029 for the full year of 2028. However, as previously stated we request the compliance date be extended 36 months for Medicaid and CHIP FFS and subsequently the metric reporting be extended to after the first full year following the API compliance date.
Prior Authorization Metrics for Drugs:
This would be a new requirement for our prior authorization vendor and our Managed Care plan which would necessitate contract amendments and potentially increased costs.
Appeals are processed by the legal division within the state and prior authorization requests are processed by our prior authorization vendor. This would require clear guidance on the definition of appeal versus resubmission, including if the request is initiated with the PAAppealRequest functionality within the standards or when an appeal is filed with our legal department in any various method. We would need to dedicate additional staffing time to coordinate a report on approvals after appeal.
Reporting a determination percentage without additional context may be misinterpreted. We may require prior authorization on drugs and have a very high approval rate simply because providers request a prior authorization determination from us prior to agreeing to purchase the drug. Conversely, there may be a very low approval rate for a high-cost drug that offers no additional benefit than an alternative low-cost drug, such as drugs designed to avoid NADAC and SMAC pricing by slightly modifying the formulation in a non-clinically meaningful way.
Prior Authorization Timeframe for Drugs:
We request the proposed rule for Medicaid and CHIP FFS to require response by 24 hours and require determination by 1 business day following receipt of all information to process the request. This update would align with section 1927(d)(5)(A) of the Act and the proposed language for 42 CFR 431.80(a)(2)) without reducing access to medications as a 72-hour supply of medications in emergency situations is already required.
This distinction between response and determination would increase quality of prior authorization reviews and decrease administrative denials as we prefer to contact prescribers for simple additional information needed to process the prior authorization request rather than deny for missing information and require the prescriber to resubmit the request. Prescribers are typically not available on weekends and holidays, which would necessitate a denial for missing information if determination is required within 24 hours, even if it could otherwise be obtained by a simple phone call during business hours (e.g., weight or height).
This distinction would reduce staffing burdens on states which are already experiencing strain with other proposed rule requirements and competing federal priorities. With the current proposed rule as written, a decision is required on major holidays and weekends even when most prescribers' offices are closed and will not act on the determination until at minimum, the next business day. Recruitment and retention of quality employees is difficult for states with limited budgets and an attractive benefit this requirement prevents is the ability to work business hours. Updating the language in the proposed rule would align with most prescriber's office hours without undue burden on states.
We request an exception to extend the determination timeframe. This allowance for an extension would decrease requests simply to meet the determination deadline, increasing administrative burden to payors and prescribers by allowing time to research complex clinical information that has been provided in a request for an exception to our policy, or to consult our medical director's opinion.
Thank you for the opportunity to comment on this proposed rule.

# Comment Analysis Template: CMS-2026-1255-0001

## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** North Dakota Medicaid / North Dakota Department of Health and Human Services
- **Stakeholder type:** Government
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** State Medicaid and CHIP Fee-for-Service program experience; pharmacy program and prior authorization operations.

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

North Dakota Medicaid argues state Medicaid and CHIP FFS programs cannot meet the October 1, 2027 compliance date because of budget constraints, procurement barriers, vendor readiness issues, and competing federal IT mandates. The commenter requests an upfront 36-month delay, funding and procurement support, a 2-business-day API update window, delayed metrics reporting after the first full year of API use, clearer appeals/resubmission guidance, and revised drug PA timing rules distinguishing response from final determination.

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** PA-DRUG-PHARMACY; PA-DRUG-MEDICAL; FHIR-IG-REQUIRED; API-USAGE-METRICS; PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS; STATE-EXTENSION-PROCESS; GENERAL metrics and implementation concerns.
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** Section 1927(d)(5)(A) of the Act; 42 CFR 431.80(a)(2); CMS-0057-F.
- **Standards referenced:** NCPDP Telecommunication Standard D.0 to F6; NCPDP SCRIPT; NCPDP Formulary & Benefit (F&B); NCPDP Real-Time Prescription Benefit (RTPB); FHIR Prior Authorization API standards; PAAppealRequest; WCAG 2.2; 11-digit to 12-digit NDC transition.

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: Upfront 36-month delay for state Medicaid and CHIP FFS**
- **Provision ID:** STATE-EXTENSION-PROCESS
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Requiring states to apply for extensions creates additional paperwork when CMS already acknowledges states may need up to 36 months.
- **Specific request:** Delay the deadline by 36 months for state Medicaid and CHIP FFS programs upfront, rather than requiring extension applications.

**Topic 2: NCPDP pharmacy drug standards readiness**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-PHARMACY
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** North Dakota Medicaid has no PBM, runs a small FFS program, lacks current support for NCPDP SCRIPT, F&B, and RTPB, and has had unsuccessful procurement efforts because vendors did not respond.
- **Specific request:** Provide funding, procurement support, vendor readiness assessment, and a 36-month implementation delay.

**Topic 3: Prior Authorization API for drugs and FHIR IG implementation**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL; FHIR-IG-REQUIRED
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** The state says adding drugs is not a simple extension of existing work because its CMS-0057-F API will not yet be built and vendor adoption of FHIR standards will require procurement, contracting, development, and testing.
- **Specific request:** Extend state Medicaid/CHIP FFS compliance by 36 months and assist with funding and vendor procurement readiness.

**Topic 4: Prior authorization information update timing**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL; API-USAGE-METRICS
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Reporting prior authorization information within 1 business day may be infeasible because determinations can take up to 24 hours and exchange may require file transfer.
- **Specific request:** Change the requirement to 2 business days.

**Topic 5: API and prior authorization metrics reporting**
- **Provision ID:** API-USAGE-METRICS
- **Position:** Modify; Clarify
- **Rationale:** Metrics are new requirements for the PA vendor and managed care plan, require contract amendments, and could be misinterpreted without context.
- **Specific request:** Start metrics reporting only after the first full year of API use, define appeal versus resubmission clearly, and provide context for determination percentage reporting.

**Topic 6: Drug PA response and determination timeframes**
- **Provision ID:** PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** A same-day determination requirement can force administrative denials when prescribers are unavailable on weekends or holidays, while emergency 72-hour medication supplies already protect access.
- **Specific request:** Require a response within 24 hours and a determination within 1 business day after receipt of all information, with an exception allowing extensions for complex clinical review.

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

- **S14:** The commenter explains that non-Part D state Medicaid FFS pharmacy programs may not support NCPDP SCRIPT, F&B, or RTPB and may lack PBM infrastructure.
- **S19:** The comment directly addresses state readiness, citing no budget, budget reductions, legislative timing, procurement duration, and vendor readiness issues.
- **S20:** The commenter requests distinguishing a 24-hour response from a final determination due 1 business day after all information is received.
- **S21:** The commenter says the October 1, 2027 API timeline is not achievable for state Medicaid/CHIP FFS due to procurement, budget, and CMS-0057-F sequencing.
- **S22:** The comment cites increased vendor contract costs, re-procurement, intermediary connectivity, and staffing burden for NCPDP implementation.
- **S29:** The commenter seeks delayed API metric reporting and notes metrics requirements will require contract amendments.
- **S34:** The commenter requests that the first metric report follow the first full year of API use, with subsequent timing tied to the delayed compliance date if adopted.
- **S36:** The commenter opposes an application-based extension process and requests an automatic 36-month delay for state Medicaid and CHIP FFS.
- **S38:** The requested extension duration is 36 months.
- **S43:** The commenter asks CMS to align drug PA timeframes with Medicaid statutory requirements by requiring response within 24 hours and determination within 1 business day after all information is received.

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Automatically delay implementation by 36 months for state Medicaid and CHIP FFS programs.
2. Provide funding assistance for implementation.
3. Support vendor readiness assessment and state procurement.
4. Change the 1-business-day PA information reporting requirement to 2 business days.
5. Delay API metrics reporting until after the first full year of API use.
6. Clarify the definition of appeal versus resubmission, including PAAppealRequest and state legal appeal workflows.
7. Add context requirements or cautions for determination percentage reporting.
8. Require Medicaid/CHIP FFS PA response within 24 hours and final determination within 1 business day after receipt of all needed information.
9. Allow exceptions to extend determination timeframes for complex clinical review.

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** Unrealistic compliance timing, state budget shortfalls, vendor procurement failure, staff constraints, contract amendments, and burdensome extension paperwork.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** Administrative denials, increased state and provider burden, higher contract costs, misinterpreted public metrics, and reduced ability to recruit and retain state employees.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** No PBM, no support for NCPDP SCRIPT/F&B/RTPB, lack of intermediary vendor interest, 10% state budget reduction, legislative biennium timing, CMS-0057-F API dependency, D.0 to F6 transition, GENEROUS model rebate review, WCAG 2.2 compliance, and 12-digit NDC transition.

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:** North Dakota DHHS faces a 10% budget reduction; next legislative session ends April 2027; fiscal biennium starts July 2027; procurement could run until September 2027; earliest work start would be October 1, 2027.
- **Studies or research referenced:** Not addressed
- **Examples provided:** Prior unsuccessful procurement attempts for electronic PA intermediary services; prescriber offices closed on weekends or holidays, making missing information hard to obtain within 24 hours.

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** State Medicaid/CHIP FFS programs, North Dakota Medicaid, Medicaid expansion managed care plans, prior authorization vendors, prescribers, pharmacies, and beneficiaries.
- **Economic implications:** The comment predicts re-procurement, contract cost increases, contract amendments, and unfunded implementation needs amid a state budget shortfall.
- **Technical feasibility:** The commenter says implementation is technically and operationally infeasible on the proposed timeline because foundational APIs and vendor connectivity are not yet in place.
- **Patient care impact:** The commenter argues revised response/determination timing would preserve medication access through emergency supplies while improving review quality and reducing avoidable administrative denials.

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Concerned
- **Tone:** Technical and critical
- **Priority level:** High

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "We request the deadline be delayed by 36 months" - Context: Central implementation timeline request for state Medicaid and CHIP FFS.
2. "We currently do not have a budget" - Context: Explanation of why North Dakota cannot meet NCPDP implementation requirements.
3. "The soonest we could start work would be October 1, 2027" - Context: The state says its earliest feasible start date is the proposed compliance date.
4. "We request the requirement be changed to 2 business days" - Context: Request to modify PA information reporting timing.

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **IMPLEMENTATION-TIMELINE** - The comment repeatedly requests a 36-month delay and delayed metrics reporting.
- [x] **COST-RESOURCES** - Budget shortfall, procurement cost increases, contract amendments, and staffing strain are central concerns.
- [x] **TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY** - The state lacks NCPDP support, PBM infrastructure, API readiness, and vendor connectivity.
- [x] **STANDARDS-MATURITY** - The comment discusses NCPDP F6, SCRIPT, F&B, RTPB, FHIR, PAAppealRequest, WCAG, and NDC transition dependencies.
- [x] **STAKEHOLDER-COORDINATION** - Implementation depends on state agencies, vendors, managed care plans, prescribers, and intermediaries.
- [x] **SMALL-PAYER-IMPACT** - North Dakota describes itself as a very small FFS program with limited market leverage.
- [x] **PROVIDER-BURDEN** - The commenter warns that rigid deadlines may increase provider resubmissions and administrative denials.
- [x] **PATIENT-ACCESS** - The proposed timeframe changes are framed as preserving medication access and review quality.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** - The comment addresses current procurement, legal appeal, vendor, and prescriber-office workflows.
- [ ] **PRIVACY-SECURITY** - Not addressed.
- [ ] **HEALTH-EQUITY** - Not addressed.
- [ ] **REGULATORY-AUTHORITY** - Not addressed.
- [ ] **MEDICAL-VS-PHARMACY-BENEFIT** - Mentioned only through managed care physician-administered drugs, not a major theme.
- [ ] **TRANSPARENCY** - Not a primary theme beyond concern over metrics context.
- [ ] **VENDOR-ECOSYSTEM** - Addressed through vendor readiness and procurement, but not as a broader market analysis.
